function: Complex-valued CNN neural receiver decoding 64-point Eisenstein MBM-RIS symbols from P x K ULA snapshots under AWGN and impulse noise (p. 3, 7).
system: Reflecting RIS (R x Q elements) modulates one RF source; ULA receiver with P elements, one data stream, 39 GHz, 312 snapshots per symbol (p. 3, 7).
method: Complex-valued CNN (two Conv2D, three fully connected layers) with six activation types; supervised cross-entropy training with Adam, 200 epochs, batch 2048 (p. 7-8).
data_channel: Simulated RIS cascaded-path model (Eqs. 2-3) at 39 GHz, LOS blocked, AWGN or impulse noise (1% probability, std 10); no standard or measured channel (p. 3, 6-7).
test_conditions: Neural receivers trained and evaluated on simulated symbols of the same system, for AWGN, impulse noise and LOS plus impulse noise; SNR from -15 to +10 dB (p. 3, 7-9).
baselines: Non-learned: Arctan-Median, mean, median, Weiszfeld and Sq-estimator receivers, 64-QAM, 8-PSK, hexagonal and theoretical QAM-MBM from [9]. Learned: none compared on BER; DNN [35] only in complexity (p. 7-9).
metrics: Bit error rate and symbol error rate versus SNR; RMS magnitude and phase error of the equalizer; average power of constellations (p. 5, 8-10).
complexity: Table III (p. 6): big-O orders for the equalizer and for neural-receiver inference per epoch, compared with an RIS-based DNN [35]; CNN stated as more complex; no runtime.
q1_support: p. 7: "The IMPN was then added with 1% probability"; the channel is the paper's own RIS path model with AWGN or impulse noise (p. 3, 5). Missing: no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "Each inference of the neural receivers used 512 symbols that were iterated eight times"; evaluation uses fresh symbols of the same simulated system. Missing: no test in a noise, geometry or constellation setting not used in training.
q3_support: p. 7: "neural network (DNN) [35] is shown in Table III"; the DNN is compared only on complexity. BER and SER (Figs. 9, 12) are compared with non-learned receivers, 64-QAM and 8-PSK. Missing: an earlier learned baseline on BER or SER.
q4_support: p. 7: "The complexity of the neural receivers together with a comparative RIS-based deep neural network (DNN) [35] is shown in Table III"; Table III (p. 6) lists big-O orders for the equalizer and the neural receivers.
q5_support: p. 8: "the bare minimum number of examples, that is, 2048 symbols"; the training data are the paper's own simulated symbols. Missing: no link to code or data, and no public dataset.
notes: Included under area 1: the learned element is the complex-valued CNN neural receiver that decodes RIS-modulated symbols from P x K ULA snapshots (Figs. 9, 12); the Eisenstein constellation, the RIS phase look-up (Eq. 7), the blind equalizer and the Weiszfeld and Sq estimators are not learned. Borderline: the receiver decodes one stream and the RIS acts as the modulator, so a reviewer may judge whether this is MIMO detection. The text gives no numeric P, R or Q. It does not say whether the LOS-plus-impulse receivers of Fig. 10 were retrained, so q2 stays 0.
